stories.head: Australian MP Helen Haines critically hurt after being hit by car
stories.stand: The independent MP was struck outside her electorate office in Victoria in what Prime Minister Anthony Albanese called a deliberate act.
stories.say: Australian independent MP Helen Haines is in critical condition after a car hit her outside her office in Wangaratta on Monday. Anthony Albanese says it was no accident.
body: Helen Haines, 65, the independent MP for Indi, was hit by a Toyota Land Cruiser outside her electorate office in Wangaratta, Victoria, on Monday afternoon. She had surgery and remained in critical condition on Tuesday.

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said it appeared to be a deliberate act and that the motive was not known. Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke said witnesses described the driver striking her a second time.

Bystanders held a 43-year-old man at the scene and he was arrested. Police said a knife was found. No charges had been announced by Tuesday, and the AFP said possible state and Commonwealth offences were being considered.
Victoria Police called it an isolated incident with no known further threat. Australia's counterterrorism team is involved in the investigation. The ABC reported that Ms Haines has lost one leg.

stories.head: Kenyan cult leader Paul Mackenzie guilty over 191 Shakahola deaths
stories.stand: A Mombasa court convicted the preacher and 28 others of murder over deaths that included 190 children at a forest ranch.
stories.say: A Kenyan court has convicted preacher Paul Mackenzie and twenty-eight others of murdering a hundred and ninety-one people, most of them children, at the Shakahola forest ranch.
body: A court in Mombasa found Paul Mackenzie and 28 co-accused guilty on Monday of murdering 191 people, 190 of them children. All had pleaded not guilty in 2024.

Prosecutors said Mackenzie directed his followers to fast to death at an 800-acre ranch in Shakahola Forest, with children made to die first. The defence argued the case rested on circumstantial evidence, hearsay and inconclusive forensics.
Sentencing is set for 6 November, Citizen Digital reported. Mackenzie still faces separate manslaughter and terrorism cases, which he denies.
More than 400 bodies have been found in the area since 2023. Kenya's human rights commission put the toll at 429 in 2024.

stories.head: Houthi missiles kill dozens of recruits at Yemen army camp
stories.stand: Ballistic missiles struck a training camp in Shabwa province as the US warned its citizens across the Middle East to stay vigilant.
stories.say: Houthi missiles have hit a Yemeni government training camp in Shabwa province, with local officials saying more than fifty recruits were killed and many more wounded on Monday.
body: Houthi forces fired three ballistic missiles at the al-Alam military camp in Shabwa province on Monday, Yemeni officials said. The camp was training new recruits.

Shabwa authorities said more than 50 recruits were killed and over 200 wounded. Other military sources gave a lower early figure. Wounded were moved to Hadramout and Aden as local hospitals struggled.
The Houthi-linked Saba agency quoted a military source as saying the group targeted Saudi gatherings at the camp. The Houthis have also claimed recent attacks on targets inside Saudi Arabia.
US embassies in 12 Middle East countries issued security alerts on Monday, warning of possible escalation and travel disruption linked to the Houthis and Iran.

stories.head: UN food agency cuts monthly aid to 500,000 people in Gaza
stories.stand: The World Food Programme says a funding shortfall forces it to shrink rations and drop half a million people from monthly support.
stories.say: The World Food Programme says it will stop monthly aid to half a million people in Gaza because of a funding shortfall, leaving about one point one million still receiving help.
body: The World Food Programme said on Monday it will end monthly aid for about 500,000 people in Gaza because it lacks money. Around 1.1 million people will still get food or cash.
Families still receiving food will get one parcel a month instead of two, plus a smaller bag of flour. The agency said it needs about 450 million dollars over six months for Gaza and the West Bank.
WFP country director Shaun Hughes said the cut was caused by funding, not access. About 1.4 million people in Gaza remain acutely food insecure, the agency said.
The agency halved the number it helps in the West Bank to 200,000 in September.

stories.head: Trump defends Russia sanctions waiver as Republicans push back
stories.stand: The US president says easing sanctions keeps Moscow talking, while Kyiv and senators from both parties say it helps Russia's war.
stories.say: Donald Trump says waiving new sanctions on Russia keeps Moscow at the negotiating table. Volodymyr Zelenskyy says it will hurt Ukraine, and senior Republicans have joined the criticism.
body: Donald Trump issued an executive order on Friday waiving measures under the Graham Act, a sanctions law he signed in September, two days before they were due to take effect.
On Sunday he said on Truth Social that he did not want to push Russia away from talks. He also accused Volodymyr Zelenskyy of not wanting the war to end.
Zelenskyy said the waiver would hurt Ukraine and help only Russia. Republican senators Thom Tillis and John Cornyn and Democrat Chuck Schumer criticised the decision.
On Monday Zelenskyy said Russia launched another night of missile and drone strikes, with no warning from partners. The Kremlin said any agreement needs Kyiv's participation.

stories.head: Floods in eastern Spain leave at least four dead
stories.stand: Torrential rain from Storm Adam swamped the Valencia region, cutting off towns and prompting hundreds of rescues.
stories.say: At least four people have died in floods across eastern Spain, two of them in the resort town of Oliva, after torrential rain swamped the Valencia region on Sunday and Monday.
body: At least four people have died after torrential rain hit eastern Spain from Sunday night, regional officials and emergency services said.
Two of the deaths were in the coastal town of Oliva, including a 79-year-old woman found at home. Another person drowned at a beach in Sagunto, and a woman died in Catalonia.

Some areas of the Valencia region recorded as much as 700 litres of rain per square metre. Security forces carried out hundreds of rescues, some by helicopter, and dozens of towns were told to stay indoors.
Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez pledged the government's full support. Regional authorities lifted the stay-at-home orders later on Monday.

stories.head: Florida issues arrest warrant for Cuba's Raúl Castro over 1996 shootdown
stories.stand: State charges over the downing of two Brothers to the Rescue planes add to a federal indictment unveiled in May.
stories.say: Florida has issued an arrest warrant for former Cuban leader Raúl Castro, accusing the ninety-five-year-old of a role in shooting down two civilian planes in 1996, killing four people.
body: Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier announced a state arrest warrant for Raúl Castro on Monday in Miami. Castro, 95, led Cuba from 2008 to 2018.
The charges relate to the downing of two unarmed Brothers to the Rescue planes on 24 February 1996. Four people were killed. Castro was Cuba's defence minister at the time.
Castro already faces a federal indictment over the same incident, unveiled in May. The federal prosecutor for southern Florida said the two cases run in parallel.
US authorities say the planes were over international waters. Cuban officials have long said the group's earlier flights breached Cuban airspace.

stories.head: Hoax 'Islamist' bomb threat emailed to hundreds of schools in Northern Ireland
stories.say: Police in Northern Ireland say a bomb threat emailed to up to three hundred schools on Monday was a hoax sent from abroad. Some schools closed, and Scottish schools were targeted too.
stories.stand: Police treated the emails as a hoax sent from abroad, but some schools closed and similar threats reached schools in Scotland.
body: Schools across Northern Ireland received a threatening email on Monday 19 October. Police said up to 300 schools reported getting the same message.

Education Minister Paul Givan said the email referred to Islamists and claimed there were viable devices in schools. He said the advice was that it was not a viable threat, and criticised the closure of some schools.
The PSNI said the email came from outside the UK and was being treated as a hoax. Assistant Chief Constable Ryan Henderson said the risk to the public was considered low.
Schools in several Scottish council areas also received threats on Monday. Police Scotland said these were being treated as a hoax and officers were investigating.

body: Anthony Williams, 33, pleaded guilty to wounding offences at Cambridge Crown Court on Monday 19 October. He appeared by video link from custody.
The charges relate to a stabbing on an LNER train from Doncaster to London on 1 November 2025. The train made an unscheduled stop at Huntingdon, where armed police arrested him.
Williams denies 14 counts of attempted murder. These cover the train, an incident at Pontoon Dock DLR station in London, and three people in Peterborough on 31 October.
He also admitted offences including affray at a Peterborough barber shop and stealing knives from an Asda in Stevenage. Mr Justice Calver said his trial on the remaining counts starts on 26 October.

stories.say: Three people have been found guilty of the manslaughter of army veteran Martin Chadburn, who died after being attacked outside a pub in Hull city centre in April.

body: Britney Naylor, 20, Shaytoyia Farrow, 21, and Lukasz Matusiak, 27, were found guilty of manslaughter at Hull Crown Court. Two other defendants were cleared.
Martin Chadburn, 53, was assaulted after leaving The Star pub on Carr Lane in the early hours of 19 April. He died in hospital two days later.
The army veteran worked for the charity Hull 4 Heroes. Prosecutors said a minor argument escalated into a group attack.
Detective Chief Inspector Leanne Murphy urged people to walk away from confrontations. The three will be sentenced at a later date.

stories.head: Bus passengers in England could face £100 fines for playing music aloud
stories.say: Councils in England are being urged to fine bus passengers one hundred pounds for playing music without headphones, under government guidance published on Monday.
stories.stand: New Department for Transport guidance helps councils draw up bylaws against loud music, vaping and littering on buses.
body: The Department for Transport published guidance on Monday 19 October for councils on tackling nuisance behaviour on buses. Passengers playing music out loud could face a £100 fine.
The Bus Services Act 2025 lets local transport authorities in England set and enforce their own bus rules. That power took effect on 5 August.
Each council must still make its own bylaw, which needs sign-off from the transport secretary. Authorised officers, not bus drivers, would enforce the rules.
London already has a TfL bylaw. A separate campaign will remind rail passengers that they can be fined up to £1,000.

body: Benny Gantz, chair of the Blue and White party, withdrew on Monday from Israel's Knesset election, which is due on 27 October.

He announced the move at a press conference at Kfar Maccabiah in Ramat Gan, according to the Times of Israel. Polls had consistently shown his party falling short of the threshold to enter parliament.
Gantz said he had failed to persuade enough voters and took responsibility. He repeated his call for a broad Zionist unity government spanning both blocs, and did not endorse another party.
Opposition parties welcomed the decision, while coalition figures urged small right-wing parties to step aside too. A KAN poll published on Sunday put about 30% of voters as undecided.

body: The US Justice Department announced on Monday that it had charged 28 lawful permanent residents in California with illegally registering to vote or voting.
Prosecutors said 22 are accused of voting in at least one election, including June's primary. Five allegedly only registered, and one cast a provisional ballot in 2020.

The cases follow a federal lawsuit filed on 15 October seeking to stop California and Los Angeles County processing ballots from about 20,000 people on a DOJ list. State and county officials have said the demands breach federal and state law.

First Assistant US Attorney Bill Essayli said about 113 non-citizens had been charged in 20 states in recent weeks. Attorney General Rob Bonta said the guilty should be held accountable but that fraud was not widespread.

body: Prime Minister Andy Burnham visited Aberfan on Monday, two days before the 60th anniversary of the 1966 disaster. He toured the memorial garden with survivors and Welsh Secretary Stephen Kinnock.
A colliery spoil tip collapsed onto Pantglas Junior School and nearby homes on 21 October 1966, killing 144 people, 116 of them children.
Burnham said the authorities had not treated Aberfan properly and that this should be acknowledged. He said making all remaining tips in Wales safe was critically important.
The UK government is giving the Welsh Government about £140m for coal tip safety, the Herald reported. No new policy was announced.

body: Barclays shares fell by more than 3% in London on Monday. The drop followed a Financial Times report that the Bank of England is examining claims about the bank's private credit business.

According to the report, the Prudential Regulation Authority received a complaint earlier this year. It concerned how Barclays recorded derivatives, known as total return swaps, used to finance private credit loans.

The question is whether traders misrepresented illiquid loans in a way that understated their risk. Reports say this could reduce the capital the bank must hold. The allegations have not been established as breaches.
Barclays is due to publish its third-quarter results on Thursday 22 October.

body: The FTSE 100 fell 1.1% to 10,764.69 on Monday, ending three straight sessions of gains. The FTSE 250 slipped 0.6%, ending a six-day winning run.
Miners were among the biggest drags as copper prices dipped. Anglo American fell 4.1% and Glencore 3.3%. Barclays also fell sharply after a report of Bank of England scrutiny.
Serica Energy fell 2.6% after flagging a further delay to restarting its Triton vessel. Pets at Home rose about 6.7% after a broker upgrade, and Mulberry gained after reporting higher sales.
European shares also opened lower as France counted the cost of weekend riots. UK jobs data is due on Tuesday and inflation figures on Wednesday.

stories.head: Merck KGaA agrees $1.3bn deal to buy Silence Therapeutics
stories.stand: The German group will pay $20 a share in cash, more than double Silence's previous price, for its experimental blood cancer drug.
stories.say: Germany's Merck KGaA has agreed to buy the drug developer Silence Therapeutics for about one point three billion dollars in cash, more than doubling its share price.
body: Merck KGaA of Darmstadt, Germany, has agreed to buy Silence Therapeutics in an all-cash deal. It will pay $20 for each American depositary share, valuing Silence's equity at about $1.3 billion.
The price is 130% above Silence's closing price on Friday 16 October. Silence shares rose about 125% on Monday after the announcement.
Merck is buying divesiran, an experimental gene-silencing treatment for polycythemia vera, a rare blood cancer. It plans to take the drug into a late-stage trial.
The deal will go through a UK scheme of arrangement. It needs shareholder, High Court and regulatory approval, and is expected to close in early 2027.

stories.say: National Australia Bank plans to cut up to two thousand five hundred jobs, about six per cent of its staff, by mid-2027, with fifteen hundred going before the end of this year.
body: National Australia Bank said on Tuesday it would cut up to 2,500 roles, about 6% of its workforce, by mid-2027. Up to 1,500 will go before the end of 2026.
The bank said the changes would simplify its operating model. Chief executive Andrew Irvine said there would be no material impact on customer-facing banking roles.

NAB will also reduce its use of consultants and contractors. Its statement to the stock exchange did not mention artificial intelligence. A governance expert urged the bank to be open about AI's role.
The Finance Sector Union criticised the cuts and their timing. NAB shares fell in early trading. The bank reports full-year results on 5 November.

stories.head: US homebuilder confidence falls to lowest since 2012
stories.stand: Rising mortgage rates and fuel costs pushed the NAHB builder sentiment index down to 29 in October, with 43% of builders cutting prices.
stories.say: Confidence among US homebuilders has fallen to its lowest level since 2012, with the industry index at twenty-nine in October as mortgage rates climbed above seven per cent.
body: The National Association of Home Builders' sentiment index fell three points to 29 in October. That is the lowest reading since June 2012. Economists had expected 31.
Some 43% of builders cut prices this month, the highest share since 2020, with an average cut of 6%. About 65% offered sales incentives.
NAHB chairman Bill Owens said mortgage rates had climbed well above 7% in recent weeks. He said higher fuel prices and inflation were also weakening buyer traffic.
The measure of prospective buyer traffic fell to 18, its lowest since April 2012 apart from April 2020, the association said.

stories.head: Japan launches MMX probe to bring back rock from Mars moon Phobos
stories.say: Japan has launched a probe to land on Phobos, a moon of Mars, and bring home at least ten grams of its soil. The capsule is due back over Australia in twenty thirty-one.
stories.stand: JAXA's Martian Moons eXploration mission lifted off on an H3 rocket and aims to be the first to return samples from the Mars system.
body: Japan's space agency JAXA launched its Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) probe on an H3 rocket from Tanegashima Space Center. Liftoff was at 19:41 GMT on Monday, early on Tuesday in Japan.
The spacecraft separated from the rocket about 71 minutes after launch. It is due to reach Mars in 2027 and spend about three years studying Phobos and its neighbour Deimos.
MMX plans to touch down on Phobos to collect at least 10 grams of material. A small rover built by the French and German space agencies is due to be dropped onto the moon first.
Scientists hope the samples will show whether the two moons are captured asteroids or debris from a giant impact on Mars. A capsule is planned to land in Australia in 2031.

stories.head: Bleached corals recover in seven weeks after touching healthy clones
stories.say: Stanford scientists say severely bleached corals fully recovered within seven weeks after touching healthy, genetically identical partners, which passed on vital algae.
stories.stand: A lab study found algae flowed from healthy to bleached coral through fused tissue, though the method cannot yet be used on whole reefs.
body: Researchers at Stanford University report that bleached coral fragments recovered fully within seven weeks when placed in contact with healthy fragments from the same colony.
In the experiment, five of ten pairs touched and five were kept a few millimetres apart. Every bleached fragment that touched recovered, while the separated ones died.
The corals fused and formed channels, and symbiotic algae moved across within three days. The algae then multiplied about ten times faster than in wild corals, the team said.

The method needs genetically identical corals, so it is not ready for reef restoration. The researchers want to find ways to deliver algae without direct contact. The study appears in Science Advances.

stories.head: Google cuts errors 40-fold in key quantum computing step
stories.say: Google researchers say a technique called magic state cultivation cut errors about forty-fold on their Willow quantum chip, easing a long-standing bottleneck.
stories.stand: A paper in Science reports the first hardware demonstration of a cheaper way to make the special states universal quantum computers need.
body: Google Quantum AI has demonstrated a method called magic state cultivation on its Willow superconducting processor. The work was published in the journal Science.
Magic states are needed for universal quantum computing but are costly to produce. Cultivation filters out flawed attempts, leaving a purer state.
The team reported errors about 40 times lower than for states prepared without cultivation, and a fidelity of about 99.99 per cent. Only about 8 per cent of attempts passed every check.
The researchers describe the result as a first step. They say larger demonstrations are still needed and technical challenges remain.

stories.head: Astronomers find first green star among unusually coloured white dwarfs
stories.say: Astronomers at the University of Warwick say some dying stars called white dwarfs glow green, pink or yellow, including what they call the first known green star.
stories.stand: A study of white dwarf spectra found that dense atmospheres and trace elements can give some of these stars unexpected colours.
body: Researchers at the University of Warwick modelled how white dwarfs would look to the human eye, using existing spectra and a model of colour vision.
They found one star, WD J1330+6435, appears chartreuse green. Sodium and other elements from accreted rocky material shape its colour, the team said.
Another, WD J1011+2845, about 48 light years away, may be the reddest star recorded. Carbon-rich white dwarfs tend to look pink or purple.
Of 151 white dwarfs within about 65 light years, five had unusual colours. Most look white. The study is in RAS Techniques and Instruments.

stories.say: Congo says Ebola has reached an eighth province, Nord-Ubangi, on the border with the Central African Republic. North Kivu has banned entry from Ituri for a week from Monday.

body: Congo's Health Ministry said on Sunday that the Ebola outbreak had reached Nord-Ubangi, which borders the Central African Republic. Two cases were recorded there, including one death.

North Kivu province imposed a one-week ban on people entering from Ituri, the epicentre, starting on Monday, state news agency ACP reported. It also limited vehicle passengers and suspended large gatherings.
At least 9,400 cases and more than 4,500 deaths have been recorded since the outbreak was declared in mid-May. It is caused by the Bundibugyo virus, which has no approved vaccine or treatment.
WHO Africa director Mohamed Yakub Janabi said cases were falling in some pockets but spreading geographically. In Kenya, the health ministry said 128 contacts remain in quarantine.

stories.head: GLP-1 drug users had slightly fewer complications after surgery, study finds
stories.say: A study of two million surgical patients in the US found those taking GLP-1 drugs had slightly fewer heart complications and infections afterwards, though it cannot prove cause.
stories.stand: Researchers at UTHealth Houston found small differences in outcomes, and outside experts said patients should not change their medication without advice.
body: Researchers at McGovern Medical School at UTHealth Houston analysed records of 2,028,601 adults who had elective surgery between 2016 and 2024, Newsweek reported.
Of these, 145,610 were taking GLP-1 drugs such as semaglutide. Major cardiovascular events occurred in 1 per cent of users and 1.1 per cent of non-users.
Infections after surgery affected 4.9 per cent of users against 5.3 per cent of non-users. The study is observational and cannot show the drugs caused the difference.
It did not establish when patients stopped the drugs before surgery. An independent doctor advised patients not to start or stop GLP-1 drugs without medical guidance.

body: The 17th UN biodiversity conference, COP17, opened its formal plenary in Yerevan on Monday. Nearly 200 nations are taking part, according to AFP via Arab News.
Armenian Environment Minister Hambardzum Matevosyan was elected COP17 president for a two-year term, Xinhua reported. The talks, themed "Taking Action for Nature", run until 30 October.
The meeting marks the midpoint of the 2022 Kunming-Montreal framework, which has 23 targets for 2030. A UN scorecard found progress uneven and finance falling far short.
Delegates aim to finalise a package called the Yerevan Pathway to speed up delivery, Down To Earth reported. Leaders at a summit on 16 October adopted a Yerevan Declaration calling for faster action.

body: Greenpeace International released its Well Connected report on Monday as the UN biodiversity summit began in Armenia.
It says only 3.5% of the world's ocean is fully or highly protected. At the pace seen since 1992, reaching the 30% target would take 265 years, the group said.

stories.head: Hackers hijacked AOMEI backup software updates to spread malware
stories.stand: Researchers say attackers briefly tampered with AOMEI Backupper's update servers this year to plant a backdoor on Windows machines.
stories.say: Researchers say hackers briefly hijacked update servers for AOMEI's Windows backup software to plant a backdoor. Machines already infected stay compromised despite the server fix.
body: Attackers repeatedly tampered with files served by AOMEI's update systems between spring and July 2026, according to ManageEngine, Google's Threat Intelligence Group and Mandiant.

They altered two configuration files for windows of about five to ten minutes. AOMEI Backupper copies checking for updates then downloaded a downloader called CROSSROAD and a backdoor called SHINYROAD.
Google tracks the attackers as UNC7017. Victims included IT services, telecoms and higher education organisations, BleepingComputer and SC Media reported.
AOMEI said it upgraded its servers and patched vulnerabilities. ManageEngine warned that server-side fixes do not remove backdoors already installed.

body: Bon Jovi have been announced as the first headliner of BST Hyde Park 2027 in London. They will play on Thursday 24 June 2027.

The show extends the band's Forever Tour, which included three sold-out nights at Wembley Stadium. Jon Bon Jovi had major vocal cord surgery in 2022. More acts will be announced later.

body: The Simpsons brought back Apu Nahasapeemapetilon in a Halloween episode, The Revengening, that aired on Sunday 18 October, NME reported.

Hank Azaria voiced Apu for decades but said in 2020 he would stop. A 2017 documentary, The Problem With Apu, had examined the stereotypes behind the character.
Co-showrunner Matt Selman said the team wanted the character to return in a way that let him evolve.

stories.head: Dealer suggests ancient Egyptian bronze may have inspired the Oscar
stories.say: A London dealer says a twenty-seven-hundred-year-old bronze of the Egyptian god Ptah, once owned by William Randolph Hearst, may have inspired the Oscar, but admits he can't prove it.
stories.stand: An antiquities dealer linked a Hearst-owned figure to Oscar designer Cedric Gibbons, but concedes there is no proof.
body: A bronze figure of the Egyptian creator god Ptah, about 2,700 years old, sold at Frieze Masters in London for an undisclosed sum, Euronews reported.
The figure was once owned by the newspaper magnate William Randolph Hearst. Antiquities dealer Rupert Wace found the link while researching its provenance.
Wace notes that Cedric Gibbons, who designed the Oscar statuette in 1928, was a friend and visitor of Hearst. He says the resemblance is striking but concedes it cannot be proved.
Gibbons died in 1960 and never publicly said what inspired his design.

stories.head: Tottenham beat Coventry 3-1 for first Premier League win of season
stories.say: Tottenham won their first Premier League game of the season on Monday night, beating Coventry three-one. James Maddison, Omar Marmoush and Ben Davies scored.
stories.stand: Spurs ended a long wait for a league win and climbed out of the relegation zone, one place above Coventry.
body: Tottenham beat Coventry City 3-1 at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on Monday night, their first Premier League win of the season.
James Maddison opened the scoring in the 14th minute on his first start since May 2025. Jack Rudoni equalised for Coventry four minutes after half-time.
Omar Marmoush restored the lead in the 58th minute with his first goal for the club, and Ben Davies added a third in stoppage time.
The result lifts Roberto De Zerbi's side to 16th, one place above Frank Lampard's Coventry. Dejan Kulusevski returned from a long injury absence as a substitute, Arab News reported.

stories.say: Cristiano Ronaldo has been suspended for thirty days and fined two hundred and fifty-five euros for walking out of Portugal's camp. The ban is backdated, so he can return in November.
stories.stand: Portugal's football federation sanctioned its captain on Monday, but the suspension is backdated and he misses no further matches.
body: The Portuguese Football Federation's disciplinary council suspended Cristiano Ronaldo for 30 days and fined him 255 euros on Monday 19 October.
It found the 41-year-old guilty of one intentional offence under Article 160(1) of its disciplinary rules.

Ronaldo left the squad in Copenhagen before a Nations League match against Denmark, after being an unused substitute in a 2-1 win over Norway. He accused coach Jorge Jesus of breaking promises about his role, which Jesus denied.
Fox Sports and Goal reported the ban is backdated to 30 September, leaving him available for Portugal's next match on 14 November. Ronaldo has apologised to his teammates.

stories.say: Britain's Sonay Kartal lost the Wuhan Open final to Poland's Maja Chwalinska on Sunday, but the run lifts her from a hundred and seventieth into the world's top fifty.
stories.stand: Chwalinska came from a set down to win her first WTA title; both finalists then withdrew from their next events with injuries.
body: Maja Chwalinska beat Sonay Kartal 2-6, 6-4, 6-2 in the Wuhan Open final on Sunday 18 October, winning her first WTA title.
Kartal, ranked 170th, reached her first WTA 1000 final unseeded after more than six months out with a stress fracture in her back. The run takes her into the top 50.
Chwalinska, the 25-year-old Polish 16th seed, beat Iga Swiatek in the semi-finals. She rises from 22nd to a career-high 11th.
On Monday, Chwalinska withdrew from the Ningbo Open with a left thigh injury, and Kartal pulled out of the Japan Open with a right knee injury, Yahoo Sports reported.
